curriculum.subject: English Language Activities
curriculum.outcomeText: identify words with -ed and - d from a text

interactions.prompt: Yesterday, Akinyi ___ to school. Find the word ending in -ed.
interactions.feedback: Yes! Walked ends in -ed and tells about yesterday.
interactions.retryHint: Look carefully at the last two letters.

interactions.prompt: Read: 'Kamau played and smiled.' Which word ends in -d?
interactions.feedback: Correct! Smile already ends in e, so the past word adds d: smiled.
interactions.retryHint: Find the word whose final added letter is d.

interactions.prompt: Sort the words by their ending.
interactions.tapAlternative: Tap a word, then its ending group.
interactions.feedback: Brilliant detecting! You spotted both past-tense endings.
interactions.retryHint: Words based on wave and live already have e, so only d is added.

interactions.prompt: Read: 'We cleaned the class and planted a tree.' Which two words end in -ed?
interactions.feedback: Exactly! Cleaned and planted both end in -ed.
interactions.retryHint: Scan the text for words ending with the letters e-d.

interactions.prompt: Sort words from the school story into Past-action word or Other word.
interactions.tapAlternative: Tap a word, then its group.
interactions.feedback: Excellent! You can find past-action words inside a text.
interactions.retryHint: Look for action words ending in -ed or -d.

interactions.prompt: Which line contains two words with the target endings?
choices: Naliaka waved and greeted her aunt.
interactions.answer: Naliaka waved and greeted her aunt.
interactions.feedback: Case solved! Waved adds -d and greeted adds -ed.
